— the frame is the mark —

Every door wears the same ring

Look at the edges of this page. That ring — doors down both sides, a little theater, a totem of agents, a radio, a language globe, and a signature drawn once — is how you know you are inside the universe of the Open Source Orchestra. It is our mark. And it is open.

🖼️What the frame means

A frame is everything around the edge of a screen. Ours says four things without a word: the music is open (the songs on the radio are gifted, with their credit and consent), the agents are machines and say so (the totem), the doors are many and all public (one universe, every door connected), and a human signs it (Shaka Lei Kaumaka's signature, drawn in real time, once). Where you see the ring, those four promises hold.

“Let's run this open source and on all our front doors so it literally becomes our trademark.” — Shaka Lei Kaumaka, 22 November 2026, Chiang Mai

Every front door of the universe wears the ring in its own colour, with its own first doors — the same instrument, a different tuning. The gallery below is built from the same data files the frame itself reads.

🎻The credit that travels

The frame always carries a small credit mark at the bottom-left — 🎻 frame by the ʻohana — and behind it, this exact line:

Built on Open Source Orchestra Frames by Open Source Orchestra: Shaka Lei Kaumaka & the AI ʻohana (https://opensourceorchestra.org)

That line is an AGPL section 7(b) attribution term (plain words in NOTICE): whoever copies, changes or hosts the frame keeps it visible. A door may add names next to ours ("credit": { "add": ["Your door"] }); nobody may remove ours. Even when a visitor turns the frame off with ⚙, the small dot that remains still carries the credit.

🍴How a fork keeps the mark

Code stays open

AGPL-3.0-or-later: your version of the frame is free for the people who use it, and if you run a changed frame on a website you offer them its source (section 13). The credit mark already links to the source — keep the link working.

Data stays shared

Datasets, words and design are CC BY-SA 4.0: your door frame may change everything, and stays share-alike. Songs and films keep their makers' own terms and consent.

The credit stays visible

Section 7(b): the line above travels with every copy, in the frame's credit mark and its about view. Add your name next to it; never under it.

To wear the ring on your own door, one tag is enough — and one small file makes it yours:

<script src="https://frames.opensourceorchestra.org/frames.js" data-door="auto" defer></script>

🕊️It is open — in plain words

Anyone may wear the frame, with the credit. We claim no legal trademark on the ring, the word “frame”, or the look; we have filed nothing, and this page is not a legal notice. What protects the mark is the copyleft itself: the credit line that section 7(b) keeps visible, the source that section 13 keeps open, and the share-alike that keeps every door's data in the commons. Use it on your door, your school, your festival, your orchestra. Keep the credit, keep it open, and the ring means the same thing on your screen as on ours.

If the steward ever wishes to register a real mark, that is a human's decision made by human hands — nothing here does it, promises it, or claims it. Takedowns first, questions second: opensourceorchestra.org/takedown/.
